stages.title: Limitations of CPI
stages.sub: Work out how CPI is calculated, then see why the measure still misleads.

steps.q: One weighted item's sharp price rise pushes the index up. Does the index tell you why prices rose, or just that they did?
steps.right: Just that they did, not why
steps.wrong: It explains exactly why they rose
steps.hint: The index is a single number worked out from weighted prices. Does a single number carry a reason with it?

steps.q: A new smartphone appears, but the CPI basket was fixed last January. Will this year's basket capture spending on it straight away?
steps.right: No, not until the basket is next updated
steps.hint: The basket is only revised once a year, not the moment new products appear.

steps.q: A student and a pensioner with high heating bills are both told inflation is 4%. Does that fit either one's real costs?
steps.right: No, their real costs differ from the average
steps.wrong: Yes, it applies equally to both
steps.hint: CPI blends everyone's spending into one national figure. Do a student and a pensioner spend the same way?

steps.q: A homeowner's mortgage interest payments jump sharply this year. Does CPI's basket pick that cost rise up?
steps.right: No, mortgage interest is not included
steps.wrong: Yes, it is included like other costs
steps.hint: CPI covers goods and services people buy, but think about what kind of cost a mortgage payment is.

steps.q: A laptop costs the same as last year but has a much faster processor. Can CPI easily separate price change from a better product?
steps.right: No, it's hard to separate the two
steps.wrong: Yes, the extra quality is easy to price out
steps.hint: The price on the shelf hasn't moved, but what you get for it has changed.
